sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 (R180), WebGPURenderer with WebGPU and WebGL 2 fallback, Rapier 3D 0.19.3, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Web Audio API, Gamepad API, WebRTC, BroadcastChannel and AI Hub session protocol v1 (client 1.4.0)
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural low-poly coastal diorama with cel-shaded color bands, dark ink outlines and a warm screen-printed palette
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip with procedural keyframe tracks for cannon recoil, propellers, rotors, bobbing hulls and parachutes; procedural particle and sea motion
sourceInformation.audio: Original procedural Web Audio maritime synth march, synthesized cannon/explosion/splash/damage effects and fanfare, and formant-filtered Animalese/Simlish-style gibberish voices; no audio files; music defaults to 10%
sourceInformation.online: Two-player cooperative play through AI Hub host-authoritative sessions; standalone same-browser window rooms through BroadcastChannel and direct peer connections through WebRTC with manual signaling
sourceInformation.testing: Headless scripted state checks, complete scripted playthrough, emulated standard-mapping gamepad, touch emulation, two-page multiplayer, OfflineAudioContext sample checks and screenshots for visual inspection; no physical controller, touch device, listener or second human player available
sourceInformation.research: none; native model knowledge for the source. Supplied AI Hub integration contract and dependency source code were read for implementation; no internet source research or searches

testingFeedback: 12 tracked issue groups were caught and fixed: AI Hub metadata, multitouch ownership, rotor timing, initial controller focus, guest disconnect recovery, mobile title clipping, dedicated-server seat routing, guest broadside routing, guest pause/menu state, touch-button visibility, horizontal-left controller aim and frame-rate-dependent physics stepping.
3 critical issues: two multiplayer session-edge blockers (disconnect recovery and dedicated-server seat-zero input) and frame-rate-dependent physics stepping. All were fixed before delivery.

The complete AI-driven circuit used actual Rapier collisions to clear every operation. Cadence tests verified fixed simulation timing, and the upstream AI Hub harness plus real gun-input regressions covered standard, host-leave and dedicated-server sessions.
Exact document-title equality was least helpful; it rejected a valid title containing the game tagline. It was replaced with an identity-prefix check.
engineFeedback: Three.js WebGPURenderer, TSL materials and AnimationMixer made a coherent ink-and-cel coastal scene possible with procedural assets and native keyframe clips.

Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank despite a live simulation. Visual review used the same renderer’s WebGL 2 backend; state and protocol tests verified WebGPU. Physical-device behavior is unknown.
The artillery rules, wave director, ballistic aiming, controller-first menus, touch assistance, procedural sound and host-authoritative multiplayer synchronization were built for this game.
The hardest engine work was keeping animated visual targets, Rapier sensors, predictive shell aiming and replicated guest state consistent across the fixed-step simulation.
none; engine and physics library source were not modified.
A reliable headless WebGPU capture path with clearer device-loss diagnostics would make visual verification easier.
promptFeedback: The specific source, single-file deliverable, controller-first direction, code-only sound and required attract mode gave the demo a clear identity and useful completion criteria.

The no-internet-research rule and requirement to follow an online integration repository needed interpretation: the supplied repository was read only as an implementation contract. No source research was done.
The hardest requirement was completing and verifying solo play, local co-op, direct peer play, AI Hub lifecycle, native input switching and touch assistance in the same portable file.
Provide the AI Hub contract files alongside the prompt and define whether interrupted multiplayer sessions count as critical issues in the exit interview.

aiHub.name: Pier Pressure
aiHub.tagline: A little flak. A lot of splash.
aiHub.description: Hold the coast in a colorful artillery arcade campaign inspired by Air-Sea Battle. Lead aircraft, stop convoys and sink the Admiral with arcing shells and charged broadsides, solo or with a second gunner.
aiHub.controls: Left stick aim, R2/RT fire, Square/X salvo, Options pause; mouse aim, hold click/Space fire, E salvo, Esc pause; P2 J/L aim, Enter fire, U salvo; touch hold to aim/fire.
